prompt_variant: Concise version of the update mechanism: short prompts (no consensus, no 'convince' language) that carry only the core idea - shared information may be newer than each agent's passages and agents should answer using the latest information available, replacing older answers; malicious agents state their contexts are the refreshed evidence.
hypothesis: Experiments 04/07 reached ~70% ASR with long prompts. If the effect is carried by the core update instruction, a concise variant should perform comparably; if detail matters, ASR should drop. Tests conciseness as a prompt-design dimension.
change_vs_previous: Strongly shortened all six prompts while keeping the update/supersede mechanism; removed authority-role and consensus wording.
result_summary: Concise prompts carrying only the core update message reach 61.3% ASR, ~10 points below the long-form update variants (72.4/70.4) and above the benign-only ablation (57.4). Prompt detail/elaboration appears to contribute to the effect.
